title: Mechanism of membrane perforation in rotavirus cell entry.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded and parsed EMD-75186 (a 3D density map: 132x132x132 voxels, 3.20 Angstrom per voxel, 2,299,968 values, 788 KB compressed) and PDB entry 10ID (an atomic coordinate file, 12,873 atom lines). HEAD-checked EMD-75185 (500,768,522 bytes compressed, 512^3 voxels, 2.32 Angstrom per voxel) without downloading. Read EMDB metadata: 537 tomograms contributed 8,565 sub-volumes to EMD-75185 and 3,255 to EMD-75186. Read the full bioRxiv preprint (34 pages, CC-BY) including its Data Availability statement; it names only EMDB and PDB accessions, zero mentions of EMPIAR, zero mentions of GitHub. Searched EMDB for all depositions by these authors (10 entries) and searched EMPIAR via the EBI search API (0 hits).
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The counts of 838 tilt series/tomograms across 7 experiments, 513,900 symmetry-expanded VP4 spike sub-particles classified as 58% upright / 11% reversed / 31% empty, membrane-overlap factors computed from MemBrain segmentations, and the GCaMP calcium-imaging time series. None of these per-particle tables, segmentations, or raw tomograms are deposited anywhere I could find.

a1_downloadable.note: What exists downloads freely and anonymously: I opened EMD-75186 and PDB 10ID. But only 2 averaged density maps plus 2 atomic models are public; the 838 tomograms and per-particle tables are not deposited (no EMPIAR entry, confirmed in the paper's own Data Availability statement and in the EMDB cross-references).

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAIL. There is no table at all, so no label column. The only plausible target - the per-spike class (upright / reversed / empty) and its membrane-overlap value - exists only inside the authors' private RELION and MemBrain output files; reproducing it would mean redoing the entire tomography pipeline on data that was never released.

a3_inputs_present.note: FAIL by the same route. The model inputs would be 3D sub-volumes cropped from the 838 tomograms; those tomograms are absent. The two public maps are averages of thousands of sub-volumes, not the individual examples.

a4_units_stated.note: Units are clear where data exists: voxel spacing in Angstroms in the map headers (3.20 and 2.32), coordinates in Angstroms in the coordinate file. Checked in the downloaded files.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL. Four public files (2 density maps, 2 atomic models) versus the ~1,500-row minimum. The 513,900 classified sub-particles reported in the paper are not obtainable.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: 0.5 GB for the two public maps; the unreleased raw tilt series would be multi-terabyte
a6_fits_laptop.note: The public files fit a laptop easily (I parsed the 9 MB uncompressed map in memory). The data an ML project would actually need - 838 tilt series at 41 tilts each - would be terabytes and is not available anyway.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Counts agree where checkable: EMDB metadata says 8,565 sub-volumes from 537 tomograms for EMD-75185, matching the preprint's 'selected 8,565 particles ... in 537 of the 838 acquired tomograms'.

a8_label_provenance.note: FAIL in principle. The would-be label (spike conformation class) is itself the output of RELION 3D classification, i.e. an unsupervised model's assignment, and the membrane-contact feature comes from MemBrain, a pretrained neural network. Training on those labels would be distilling two existing pipelines, not learning from a physical measurement.

existing_models.name: MemBrain-seg (deep-learning membrane segmentation for cryo-electron tomograms; v2 2024)
existing_models.score_and_split: Not re-measured by me; the paper itself ran the pretrained checkpoint MemBrain_seg_v10_beta on all 838 tomograms, which is a working endorsement rather than a benchmark number.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Not retrieved - I found MemBrain only through this paper's methods and a search result list, not by reading its paper.

existing_models.name: DeepETPicker (weakly supervised 3D particle picking, Nature Communications 2024)
existing_models.score_and_split: Reported as fast and accurate on cryo-electron tomography picking benchmarks; I read only the search-result summary, not the numbers.

existing_models.name: DeepFinder / DeePiCt / TomoTwin (deep-learning localisation and classification of molecules in tomograms)
existing_models.score_and_split: DeepFinder reported best overall localisation in the SHREC2019 simulated-tomogram challenge; TomoTwin is pretrained on 120 protein structures and needs no annotation. From search summaries only.

backbone.name: None applicable - no 3D cryo-electron tomography foundation model with open weights fits sub-volume classification here, and there is no data to fit a head on
backbone.licence: EMDB maps and PDB coordinates are public domain; preprint is CC-BY 4.0

integration.partner_dataset: EMPIAR (the public archive of raw electron-microscopy image data) would be the needed partner, but this study deposited nothing there
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Cannot be written: without the tomograms or the per-particle class table there is nothing to join.

controls.positive_control: Would have been: recover the published 58% upright / 11% reversed / 31% empty split of spike conformations - but the per-spike assignments are not public.
controls.negative_control: Label shuffling, not runnable without labels.
controls.external_validation: None; no second tomography dataset of rotavirus entry with released per-particle states exists that I found.

honest_claim_h3: No honest claim is possible: the public release is two averaged density maps and two atomic models, from which no per-example prediction task can be built.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use small 3D cryo-tomogram cubes to predict whether a rotavirus spike is upright, flipped, or absent, and whether it touches a membrane.
plain_idea.train_on: The project I considered would train on cropped 3D sub-volumes around each of the 513,900 spike positions the authors analysed, one example per spike position, with the tomogram or experiment as the grouping variable. Verified count of publicly available examples: 0.
plain_idea.predict: The spike's conformational class (upright, reversed, or empty) plus its membrane-overlap value. The true answer comes from the authors' RELION 3D classification and MemBrain membrane segmentation of cryo-electron tomograms - both computational assignments, not direct measurements.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Structural virology labs doing in-cell tomography would get an automatic reader of entry states instead of weeks of manual classification; even a failure would tell us how far sub-volume classifiers transfer between viruses. None of it is possible because the inputs and labels were never released.

more_or_better_data.why: Nothing usable is released: 2 maps and 2 coordinate files, versus simulated and real tomogram benchmarks (SHREC challenge, DeepETPicker's datasets) that are fully public with annotated particles.

confidence_score.why: No per-particle data, no replicate structure, so no way to estimate per-prediction uncertainty.

models_beatable.why: MemBrain-seg (2024), DeepETPicker (2024), TomoTwin and DeePiCt are recent, open and actively used - this very paper depends on MemBrain's pretrained weights.

guaranteed_improvement.why: Fails the first condition: we cannot even assemble the training set, let alone run the existing models on the same split.

ml_idea: Considered and abandoned: classify 3D sub-volumes cropped around rotavirus spike positions in in-cell cryo-electron tomograms into upright / reversed / empty conformations and predict membrane engagement, as an automatic replacement for RELION classification plus MemBrain segmentation. Dead on arrival because neither the tomograms nor the per-particle class assignments were deposited.

effort.compute_note: Only the two public maps were sized (0.5 GB compressed total, one of them parsed in memory at 9 MB). No feature-table estimate is meaningful because the required raw tomograms are unavailable and would be multi-terabyte if they were.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Read the Data Availability statement and search EMPIAR for a raw-data deposition - took five minutes and killed it: EMDB and PDB accessions only, zero EMPIAR entries.

verdict_reason: Beautiful biology, but the public release is four files - two averaged cryo-electron tomography maps (one 512-voxel-cubed, one 132-voxel-cubed, both of which I opened or sized) and two atomic models. The 838 tomograms, the 513,900 classified spike sub-particles, the membrane segmentations and the calcium-imaging traces that would form any feature/label table are not deposited anywhere, so A2 (no label column exists), A3 (inputs absent) and A5 (4 rows, not 1,500) all fail. A8 would also fail even if the table existed, because the class labels are RELION classification output and the membrane feature is MemBrain neural-network output - training on them distils two existing tools rather than learning biology.
